document_summary: California Business and Professions Code § 16729 (AB 325), a Justia mirror of the statute prohibiting use or distribution of a common pricing algorithm in restraint of trade, applying statewide in California.

rules.title: Common pricing algorithm prohibition (Cartwright Act amendment, AB 325)
rules.requirement: It is unlawful to use or distribute a common pricing algorithm as part of a contract, combination or conspiracy in restraint of trade, or to use or distribute one while coercing another person to adopt its recommended price or commercial term. The statute is general and does not mention housing or rent specifically, but a pricing algorithm using competitor data to influence prices would reach rent-setting software.
rules.key_value: Ban on using/distributing a common pricing algorithm (software using competitor data to set prices) in restraint of trade or with coerced adoption
rules.coverage_conditions: Applies to any 'person' (as defined in Bus. & Prof. Code § 16702), excluding end consumers. 'Common pricing algorithm' means any methodology, including a computer, software, or other technology, used by two or more persons that uses competitor data to recommend, align, stabilize, set, or otherwise influence a price or commercial term.
rules.exemptions: End consumers of a product or service are not covered 'persons'.
rules.interaction: Does not impair or limit the applicability of antitrust laws (the Cartwright Act provisions of this part). General statewide antitrust provision; not rent-specific, so local algorithmic rent-setting ordinances (e.g., Berkeley, San Francisco) may operate in addition.
rules.quoted_span:
(a) It shall be unlawful for a person to use or distribute a common pricing
algorithm as part of a contract, combination in the form of a trust, or conspiracy to
restrain trade or commerce in violation of this chapter.
rules.extraction_notes: Added by Stats. 2025, Ch. 338, Sec. 1 (AB 325), effective January 1, 2026, per the document. Justia mirror of the statute. Statute is a general antitrust provision and does not expressly mention rent or housing.
